Q: Can't get running instance of Outlook and New Interop.Outlook.Application opens Outlook as administrator not windows user A:

Are you forcing your project to run as x64?

You can't and don't want to use ANY CPU, since then what bit size your application runs as is "left to the wind and chance". So, force your project to also run and match the bit size of office, and no code changes should be required.

In other words, the fact of changing from x32 office to x64 bits should not change anything, but DOES require you to change the bit size of your running .net application to match the same bit size used for office.

Edit: You cannot use the new version of outlook

Having stated all of the above, keep in mind that office builds now have a option to use the "new" outlook, and that new version of outlook does not support COM object automation. That means CreateObject, and GetObject can't work, and will not work.

That option is this:

So, if this option is turned on, then x32 or x64 bit office and Outlook does NOT matter, it will NOT work no matter what you do.

Q: How to Find best match using hashset(Of String) ignore case A:

The HashSet(Of T) class has a constructor that let you specify the comparer. The same applies to the LINQ method ToHashSet.

Dim comparer As IEqualityComparer(Of String) = StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase
Dim strCompareHash As HashSet(Of String) = stringToCompare.
    Split(Microsoft.VisualBasic.ChrW(32)).
    ToHashSet(comparer)

The whole method could be rewritten with LINQ to be more compact:

Public Shared Function FindBestMatch(ByVal stringToCompare As String, ByVal strs As IEnumerable(Of String)) As String
    Dim comparer As IEqualityComparer(Of String) = StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase
    Dim strCompareHash As HashSet(Of String) = stringToCompare.Split(ChrW(32)).ToHashSet(comparer)
    return strs.
        Select(Function(s) (Str:=s, Tokens:=s.Split(ChrW(32)))).
        OrderByDescending(Function(x) strCompareHash.Intersect(x.Tokens, comparer).Count()). 
        First().Str
End Function

This assumes that strs is never null or empty, you might want to ensure that and return Nothing early. It would also be good to add an (optional) parameter to be able to pass the IEqualityComparer(Of String).

Q: Inject Custom Variable into ngx_http_fastcgi_module at Runtime from a Third-Party Module A:

No, not for arbitrary FastCGI param names at pure request runtime.

"ngx_http_fastcgi_module" builds the FastCGI PARAMS record inside

"ngx_http_fastcgi_create_request()".

If the param name is not already known by the FastCGI module, another third-party module cannot cleanly add this at runtime: MY_VAR=hello, without patching or replacing the ngx_http_fastcgi_module.c.

There are two practical alternatives.

1. Use r->headers_in for HTTP_* params

In ngx_http_fastcgi_module.c, notice the function:

ngx_http_fastcgi_create_request()

Inside that function, NGINX reads request headers from:

r->headers_in

and converts them into FastCGI params using this pattern:

HTTP_ + uppercase(header name, with "-" changed to "_")

For example:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer testtoken123" http://example.com/

can be visible in PHP as:

$_SERVER["HTTP_AUTHORIZATION"]

because FastCGI converts request headers like this:

Authorization -> HTTP_AUTHORIZATION
X-My-Var      -> HTTP_X_MY_VAR
User-Agent    -> HTTP_USER_AGENT

So a third-party module can add or modify request headers before ngx_http_fastcgi_create_request() runs.

The limitation is that this only gives HTTP_* params, not arbitrary names like MY_VAR.

2. Use a generated include with dynamic NGINX variable values

Keep one static include in nginx.conf:

location ~ \.php$ {
    fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php-fpm.sock;
    include /path/generated_fastcgi_params.conf;
}

Generate that file automatically:

fastcgi_param MY_VAR $my_var;
fastcgi_param APP_ENV $app_env;

Then your module can set the value of $my_var and $app_env dynamically at request runtime.

So the final rule is:

FastCGI param names must exist before ngx_http_fastcgi_create_request() runs.
FastCGI param values can be dynamic set in run time handler.

This allows behavior similar to Apache mod_env / SetEnv, without patching
ngx_http_fastcgi_module, but new param names require to be set first in include file in nginx.conf , you can inject that in config time dynamically via preconfiguration from conf buffer,etc
